name: Crescens
overview: Crescens is a male figure mentioned in the New Testament as a companion of the Apostle Paul. He is uniquely noted for having been sent to Galatia, indicating his role in the early Christian mission. No additional tribal or familial details are provided about him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Crescens appears once in Scripture without any specified meaning or title. It is presented simply as a proper name without further elaboration on its significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Crescens beyond his association with Paul as a companion who was sent to Galatia.
scriptureSignificance: Crescens holds significance as a trusted companion of Paul, entrusted with the important task of ministering in Galatia. His mention reflects the expanding missionary efforts of the early church and Paul's reliance on fellow workers to spread the gospel. Though briefly noted, Crescens represents faithful service in the propagation of Christ's message.
